---
name: halfsize
description: Compress a video to an exact target size (20 MB, 16 MB, 700k, ...) on the local machine with FFmpeg, then verify quality with VMAF/SSIM. Use when a user needs a video to fit a platform cap, asks to "make this smaller", or wants to know what a size cut costs in quality.
---

# halfsize

`halfsize` is a local CLI. It does the bitrate math, picks a resolution, encodes twice,
and reports the measured quality. It never uploads the file.

## When to use this

- "Make this fit in 25 MB" / "Discord won't take it" / "WeChat says the file is too big"
- "Compress this but don't ruin it" — run it and report VMAF instead of guessing
- "How small can this go?" — try a target and read the verdict

## Commands

```bash
# exact size
npx halfsize input.mp4 --to 25mb

# let a platform cap pick the size
npx halfsize input.mp4 --for discord
npx halfsize input.mp4 --for gmail     # 18 MB, safe under the 25 MB message cap
npx halfsize input.mp4 --for outlook   # 15 MB, safe under the 20 MB message cap

# several files, one command
npx halfsize a.mp4 b.mp4 c.mp4 --to 10mb

# smaller, at the cost of compatibility
npx halfsize input.mp4 --to 10mb --codec h265

# keep resolution, accept a worse ratio
npx halfsize input.mp4 --to 25mb --no-downscale

# no soundtrack
npx halfsize input.mp4 --to 10mb --no-audio

# inspect the plan without encoding
npx halfsize input.mp4 --to 25mb --dry-run --json

# machine-readable result (plan, accuracy, VMAF, SSIM)
npx halfsize input.mp4 --to 25mb --json
```

With more than one input, `--json` returns `{ "files": [ ... ] }`.

If `npx halfsize` is unavailable, use `npx github:YKLovePython/halfsize` with the same flags.

## How to read the result

- `0.3% under target` — good; it deliberately aims slightly under hard caps
- `VMAF >= 90` — looks the same; `80-90` — slight softening; `< 70` — visible loss
- The JSON result includes `output.file`, `output.bytes`, `quality.vmaf`, `quality.ssim`,
  `accuracy`, and `verdict`.

## Rules

- Do not upload the user's video anywhere, and do not suggest an online compressor as a first step.
- Do not promise "no quality loss". Report the measured VMAF/SSIM and the verdict.
- If the source is already smaller than the target, stop and tell the user instead of re-encoding.
- HDR sources (iPhone HLG, HDR10/PQ) are tone-mapped to SDR automatically. Do not warn about washed-out colors unless the user asks to keep HDR.
- If the target is below the minimum the duration can hold, the CLI exits with the smallest achievable size. Report that number and suggest a larger target or trimming, instead of rerunning with `--force`.
- Prefer H.264 unless the user asks for smaller files or accepts H.265 compatibility tradeoffs.
- Write the output next to the input unless the user asks for a specific `--out` path.

halfsize

Compress any video to any size. Locally. And keep the quality.

中文说明 · Website & guides · Quick start · How it works · FAQ

As featured in 阮一峰《科技爱好者周刊》第 418 期 · 1,900+ downloads a week on npm

New in 0.1.10: the first run on macOS no longer reports a missing FFmpeg. The bundled ffprobe is a 76 MB binary, and macOS can spend more than ten seconds scanning it before the first launch. The old six-second check called that a failure. Release notes

--- WeChat and Discord both stop at **20 MB**. Email chokes around the same. So you open a video editor, guess a bitrate, export, check the size, export again, and still can't tell whether the picture got worse. `halfsize` turns that into one command: ```bash npx halfsize wedding.mp4 --to 25mb ``` It computes the bitrate, picks the resolution that actually fits, encodes twice, then measures the result with **SSIM** and **VMAF** so you know whether it still looks the same. ``` halfsize 0.1.10 source.mp4 23.2 MB 8s 1920x1080 30.00 fps h264 target 2.00 MB plan H.264 960x540 1.81 Mbps audio 128 kbps 2-pass scale 1920x1080 -> 960x540 estimate 1.94 MB (12x smaller) output source.2mb.mp4 measuring quality done in 1s 23.2 MB -> 1.99 MB 12x smaller 0.4% under target VMAF 84.4 SSIM 0.968 slight softening -> C:\Videos\source.2mb.mp4 ``` ## Why this exists "Make it smaller" is a solved problem. **"Make it fit in exactly 20 MB, and tell me if it still looks right"** is the part every tool makes you guess at. - HandBrake is excellent, but it asks you to think in codecs, RF values, and presets. - Online compressors work until you remember you just uploaded a private video to a stranger. - `ffmpeg` can do all of this. Nobody remembers the 11 flags, and almost nobody checks VMAF afterwards. `halfsize` is the missing 5%: a target size you type, and a quality score you can read. | | halfsize | HandBrake | Online compressors | |---|---|---|---| | Fit an exact size | ✅ one flag | manual bitrate math | usually re-encodes blindly | | Tells you the quality cost | ✅ VMAF + SSIM | ❌ | ❌ | | Your file stays on your machine | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | | Scriptable / CI friendly | ✅ CLI + JSON | ❌ GUI | ❌ | | Learns a new UI | no | yes | yes | ## Quick start Requires [Node.js 18+](https://nodejs.org). FFmpeg is bundled on first install; if it cannot be downloaded, `halfsize` uses your system install instead. ```bash # compress to a size npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb # or just name the app you are uploading to npx halfsize video.mp4 --for discord # several files in one go npx halfsize clip1.mp4 clip2.mp4 clip3.mp4 --to 10mb # smaller file, same quality budget npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 10mb --codec h265 # quality-first mode when size does not matter npx halfsize video.mp4 --crf 23 # preview the plan without encoding npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb --dry-run # machine-readable, for scripts npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb --json ``` Install it globally if you will use it more than once: ```bash npm install -g halfsize ``` ### In CI The same compression runs in GitHub Actions, and the quality report lands in the build log: ```yaml - uses: YKLovePython/halfsize-action@v1 with: files: artifacts/recording.mp4 args: --to 20mb ``` [halfsize-action on the GitHub Marketplace](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/halfsize-compress-video-to-an-exact-size). ### The local web app ```bash npx halfsize --web ``` Opens `http://127.0.0.1:4174` — drag a video in, pick 20 MB / 16 MB / 5 MB or type your own limit, and watch the encode. The file goes to a temporary folder **on your own machine**; nothing is sent anywhere.

After each run you can download a **share card** (the image at the top of this README) with the real numbers on it. Step-by-step guides with measured quality numbers: [Discord 20 MB](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/discord/) · [WhatsApp 16 MB](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/whatsapp/) · [WeChat 20 MB](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/wechat/) · [email attachments](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/email/) · [X / Twitter](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/twitter/) · [any 20 MB limit](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/20mb/) · [FFmpeg target size](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/ffmpeg-compress-to-size/) · [compress without uploading](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/offline/). ### Which size do I need? | Where it is going | The cap | Command | |---|---|---| | Discord (free) | 20 MB per file | `--for discord` | | WeChat chat video | 20 MB | `--for wechat` | | WhatsApp, sent as media | 16 MB | `--for whatsapp` | | Gmail attachment | 25 MB message → 18 MB file | `--for gmail` | | Outlook / corporate mail | 20 MB message → 15 MB file | `--for outlook` | | X / Twitter | 512 MB | `--for twitter` | | Anything else | whatever you type | `--to 700mb` | The email rows are smaller on purpose: base64 makes the attachment about 37% bigger than the file, so an 18 MB MP4 is what fits in a 25 MB message. Caps change; `--to` always overrides the preset. Full table, with what each cap counts and the measured VMAF at each size: [size limits by platform](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/file-size-limits/) · [every target size explained](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/compress-video-to-size/) · [video size calculator](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/video-size-calculator/). ### Use it from an agent The repo ships a skill in [`skills/halfsize/SKILL.md`](skills/halfsize/SKILL.md). Install it with the [skills CLI](https://skills.sh) so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and the rest pick it up automatically: ```bash npx skills add YKLovePython/halfsize ``` Or copy the folder into your agent's skills directory by hand (for Claude Code: `.claude/skills/halfsize/`). Either way the agent can turn "make this fit in 25 MB" into a compression plus a measured quality report, instead of guessing a bitrate. ## How it works 1. **Probe.** Read duration, resolution, frame rate, audio bitrate, rotation, and HDR metadata. 2. **Budget.** Total bitrate = target bytes × 8 ÷ duration, minus audio, minus a small container overhead. 3. **Pick a resolution.** Walk a ladder from the source size down to 240p and choose the largest one whose pixels fit the budget at that codec's bits-per-pixel target (H.264: 0.072 bpp, H.265: 0.045 bpp). This is why a 12× shrink still looks reasonable: the encoder gets to spend its bits on fewer pixels. 4. **Encode twice.** Two-pass ABR with `libx264` or `libx265`. Pass one learns where the bits are needed; pass two spends them. Output is `yuv420p`, AAC audio, `+faststart`, and tagged `hvc1` for H.265 so it plays on Apple devices. HLG/PQ sources are tone-mapped to SDR BT.709 in the same pass; without that, 8-bit pixels keep their HDR tags and look grey. 5. **Prove it.** Sample three points in the video, compute SSIM at each, and VMAF at the midpoint. Compare against thresholds and print a verdict in plain language. ``` VMAF ≥ 95 indistinguishable VMAF ≥ 90 looks the same VMAF ≥ 80 slight softening VMAF ≥ 70 visible loss below 70 clearly degraded ``` VMAF is Netflix's perceptual metric; it correlates with human judgement far better than PSNR or bitrate. It is not magic, but it is a much better answer than "trust me". ## What each size costs Same 60-second 1080p clip, default settings, measured on a normal laptop: | Target | Output | Resolution | Video bitrate | VMAF | Verdict | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 20 MB | 19.45 MB | 1280×720 | 2.46 Mbps | 88.3 | slight softening | | 16 MB | 15.59 MB | 960×540 | 1.94 Mbps | 84.8 | slight softening | | 10 MB | 9.77 MB | 960×540 | 1.17 Mbps | 82.9 | slight softening | | 5 MB | 4.93 MB | 640×360 | 0.55 Mbps | 72.0 | visible loss | Source: 60 s, 1920×1080, 30 fps, 18 Mbps H.264 (136 MB). VMAF is measured against the source at the midpoint, SSIM at three points. Real numbers move with content: a talking head does much better than confetti. At 20 MB the tool picked 720p on purpose. Sixty seconds of 1080p at 2.4 Mbps looks worse than 720p at the same bits. `--no-downscale` overrides that, and `--codec h265` buys roughly 30% more quality at the same size if your player supports it. ## CLI reference ``` halfsize [options] --to Target size: 25mb, 700k, 1.5gb --for Target cap for discord, whatsapp, wechat, gmail, outlook, email, twitter --crf Quality mode instead of size mode (18 best, 23 balanced, 28 small) --codec h264 (default, maximum compatibility) or h265 (about 30% smaller) --preset ultrafast .. veryslow (default: medium) --out Output path --no-audio Drop the audio track --no-verify Skip SSIM/VMAF --no-downscale Never reduce resolution (the target may then be missed) --force Encode even when the target is below the minimum for this duration --json Machine-readable result --dry-run Print the plan, do not encode --web Start the local web app --port Port for the web app (default 4174) --doctor Show which FFmpeg and encoders were found -h, --help Help -v, --version Version ``` Sizes accept `b`, `k`/`kb`, `m`/`mb`, `g`/`gb`, with or without a space. No unit means MB. `--for` uses the current free-tier caps (checked November 2026): `discord` 20 MB, `whatsapp` 16 MB, `wechat` 20 MB, `gmail`/`email` 18 MB, `outlook` 15 MB, `twitter` 512 MB. Email caps apply to the base64-encoded message, so an 18 MB file is the largest that stays under Gmail's 25 MB. Caps change, so `--to` always overrides. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` error. `--json` returns the plan, the measured quality, and the target accuracy, which makes it easy to wrap in a script. ## Install notes Needs Node.js 18 or newer. The first `npx` run downloads both the package and a prebuilt FFmpeg, so it can pause for a minute. If you will use it more than once, install it globally and skip that wait on every run: ```bash npm install -g halfsize halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb ``` If `npx` keeps starting an old cached version, pin it: `npx halfsize@latest ...`. `ffmpeg-static` downloads a prebuilt FFmpeg during `npm install`; FFprobe ships inside `ffprobe-static`, so it needs no download. If you are behind a proxy or a TLS-inspecting network, that download can fail. Point it at a mirror, or use a build you already have: ```bash # use the npmmirror binary mirror (fast in mainland China) FFMPEG_BINARIES_URL=https://registry.npmmirror.com/-/binary/ffmpeg-static npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb # or an FFmpeg already on disk HALFSIZE_FFMPEG=/path/to/ffmpeg HALFSIZE_FFPROBE=/path/to/ffprobe npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb ``` If npm says `unable to verify the first certificate`, a proxy or antivirus is inspecting TLS. On Node 22.15+ use the system certificate store: ```powershell $env:NODE_OPTIONS="--use-system-ca"; npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb ``` A failed binary download no longer aborts the install: halfsize still starts and tells you which of these fixes to apply. On Windows, `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` is enough. On macOS, `brew install ffmpeg`. On Debian/Ubuntu, `sudo apt install ffmpeg`. Run `npx halfsize --doctor` to see what was found. ## FAQ **Does my video get uploaded?** No. The CLI never touches the network. The web app talks only to `127.0.0.1`, and uploaded files go to a temp directory that is deleted when the process exits. **How do I get a video under Discord's 20 MB limit?** `npx halfsize clip.mp4 --for discord` targets the free-tier cap (20 MB as of late 2026) and writes a normal MP4 that plays in Discord's preview. Long 1080p clips usually come out at 720p; that resolution drop is what buys the size. **WeChat says the video is too large. What now?** `npx halfsize clip.mp4 --for wechat` targets the 20 MB chat-video cap. If you need it smaller still, pass `--to 10mb` (or any size) instead. **How many minutes of video fit in 20 MB?** About two minutes at 1.2 Mbps, which is normal 720p. Five minutes only works at 400 kbps (low-motion 540p), and ten minutes leaves 133 kbps — that is a slideshow, not video. Since 0.1.9 the tool does that arithmetic before encoding and reports the smallest size the duration can hold, so you find out in a second instead of ten minutes. **Why does my iPhone video turn grey after compressing?** Because it is HDR. iPhone 12 and later record HLG by default, and older tools re-encode those values as ordinary 8-bit video while keeping the HDR tag, so players show it flat and washed out. halfsize detects HLG and PQ and converts to SDR BT.709 inside the same encode pass, including the quality measurement, so the output looks like what you saw on the phone. On a version before 0.1.9, upgrade instead of tuning bitrate. **Why did it lower my resolution?** Because 20 MB of 4K is not enough bits to look good. Lowering resolution and keeping the bitrate per pixel sane almost always looks better than keeping 4K and starving it. Use `--no-downscale` if you want to override that. **Why is the output slightly under the target, not exactly on it?** Container overhead and two-pass ABR both vary a little. `halfsize` aims ~3% under so it never overshoots a hard platform cap. In the example above it landed 0.4% under. **H.264 or H.265?** H.264 plays everywhere, including old Android phones and browsers. H.265 is roughly 30% smaller at the same quality but can be awkward in some editors and older hardware. Default is H.264. **Does it work on Windows / macOS / Linux?** Yes. It is plain Node.js and FFmpeg. **Can I batch a folder?** Yes. List the files, or let your shell expand them: ```bash npx halfsize *.mp4 --to 25mb ``` Each file gets its own plan and verdict, a failure does not stop the rest, and `--json` returns `{ "files": [ ... ] }`. `--out` is allowed only when there is a single input. **Why "halfsize"?** Because the honest answer to "how much smaller will it get?" is usually "about half, or a lot more than half". The tool reports the real number either way. ## Roadmap - Hardware encoding (NVENC / QSV / VideoToolbox) as an opt-in fast path - A folder watcher that compresses new files as they appear - Subtitle and multiple audio track passthrough - AV1 (`libsvtav1`) when the source is already AV1-friendly - A single-file binary, so Node.js is not required If you want one of these, open an issue and say which. Pull requests are welcome; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Development ```bash git clone https://github.com/YKLovePython/halfsize.git cd halfsize npm install npm test node bin/halfsize.mjs --web ``` The test suite includes a real end-to-end encode: it generates a clip with FFmpeg, compresses it to a target, probes the output, and asserts the size and SSIM. No fixtures in the repo. ## License MIT. Use it, fork it, ship it. See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for what changed. --- If `halfsize` saved you from guessing a bitrate, a star helps the next person find it.

halfsize

把任何视频压缩成任意大小，并且画质不变。全程本地。

English · 官网与教程 · 快速开始 · 它怎么工作 · 常见问题

已被 阮一峰《科技爱好者周刊》第 418 期 收录 · npm 每周 1,900+ 次下载

0.1.10 更新：macOS 首次运行不再误报「找不到 FFmpeg」。内置的 ffprobe 是 76 MB，系统首次启动前会扫描一遍，可能超过十秒，旧版本的六秒超时把它当成了失败。 更新说明

--- 微信和 Discord 都只让发 **20 MB**，邮件也大多卡在 **20 MB**。 于是你打开剪辑软件，猜一个码率，导出，看一眼大小，再导一次——最后还是不知道画质到底掉了多少。 `halfsize` 把这件事变成一行命令： ```bash npx halfsize 婚礼.mp4 --to 25mb ``` 它会算码率、挑一个真正塞得下的分辨率、做两遍编码，最后用 **SSIM** 和 **VMAF** 测给你看： 画质到底还在不在。 ``` halfsize 0.1.10 source.mp4 23.2 MB 8s 1920x1080 30.00 fps h264 target 2.00 MB plan H.264 960x540 1.81 Mbps audio 128 kbps 2-pass scale 1920x1080 -> 960x540 estimate 1.94 MB (12x smaller) output source.2mb.mp4 measuring quality done in 1s 23.2 MB -> 1.99 MB 12x smaller 0.4% under target VMAF 84.4 SSIM 0.968 slight softening -> C:\Videos\source.2mb.mp4 ``` ## 为什么做这个 「把视频变小」早就有人解决了。真正没人做好的是：**「刚好塞进 20 MB，然后告诉我画质还行不行」**。 - HandBrake 很好用，但它要你想清楚编码器、RF 值、preset 这些词。 - 在线压缩网站也能用，直到你想起自己刚把私人视频传给了陌生人。 - `ffmpeg` 当然做得到，只是没人记得那 11 个参数，而且几乎没人压完再测一遍 VMAF。 `halfsize` 补的就是这最后 5%：你输入一个目标大小，它给你一个看得懂的画质分数。 | | halfsize | HandBrake | 在线压缩 | |---|---|---|---| | 精确压到指定大小 | ✅ 一个参数 | 要自己算码率 | 通常只是盲压 | | 告诉你画质代价 | ✅ VMAF + SSIM | ❌ | ❌ | | 文件留在本机 | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | | 能写进脚本 / CI | ✅ CLI + JSON | ❌ 图形界面 | ❌ | | 需要重新学一套界面 | 不用 | 要 | 要 | ## 快速开始 需要 [Node.js 18+](https://nodejs.org)。首次安装会下载 FFmpeg；下载失败时会自动使用你系统里已有的 FFmpeg。 ```bash # 压到指定大小 npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb # 或者直接说你要传到哪里 npx halfsize video.mp4 --for discord # 一次压好几个 npx halfsize clip1.mp4 clip2.mp4 clip3.mp4 --to 10mb # 更小的文件，H.265 npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 10mb --codec h265 # 不在乎大小，只想要好画质 npx halfsize video.mp4 --crf 23 # 只看方案，不真的压 npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb --dry-run # 给脚本用的 JSON npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb --json ``` 常用的话装到全局： ```bash npm install -g halfsize ``` ### 在 CI 里跑 同一套压缩可以直接放进 GitHub Actions，画质报告留在构建日志里： ```yaml - uses: YKLovePython/halfsize-action@v1 with: files: artifacts/recording.mp4 args: --to 20mb ``` [halfsize-action 的 Marketplace 页面](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/halfsize-compress-video-to-an-exact-size)。 ### 本地网页版 ```bash npx halfsize --web ``` 打开 `http://127.0.0.1:4174`，把视频拖进去，选 20 MB / 16 MB / 5 MB，或者自己输入一个数， 然后看着它压。文件只会写进**你自己电脑**的临时目录，不会发到任何地方。

每次压完可以生成一张**分享图**（就是本文最上面那张），上面是这次真实的数字。 附实测画质的分平台教程： [微信 20 MB](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/zh/wechat/) · [任意 20 MB 限制](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/zh/20mb/) · [邮件附件](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/zh/email/) · [X / Twitter](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/zh/twitter/) · [ffmpeg 指定大小](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/zh/ffmpeg-compress-to-size/) · [Discord 20 MB](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/discord/) · [WhatsApp 16 MB](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/whatsapp/) · [本地压缩不上传](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/zh/offline/)。 ### 我该压到多少？ | 发到哪里 | 上限 | 命令 | |---|---|---| | Discord（免费档） | 每个文件 20 MB | `--for discord` | | 微信聊天视频 | 20 MB | `--for wechat` | | WhatsApp（当媒体发） | 16 MB | `--for whatsapp` | | Gmail 附件 | 整封 25 MB → 文件 18 MB | `--for gmail` | | Outlook / 企业邮箱 | 整封 20 MB → 文件 15 MB | `--for outlook` | | X / Twitter | 512 MB | `--for twitter` | | 其他 | 你自己写 | `--to 700mb` | 邮件那两行故意更小：base64 会让附件比文件大约 37%，所以 25 MB 的邮件里塞得进的是一个 18 MB 的 MP4。平台上限会变，`--to` 永远能覆盖预设。完整的表，包括每个上限到底算的是什么、 每一档的实测 VMAF：[各平台文件大小上限](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/zh/file-size-limits/) · [每个目标大小能装什么](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/zh/compress-video-to-size/) · [视频大小计算器](https://YKLovePython.github.io/halfsize/zh/video-size-calculator/)。 ### 给 agent 用 仓库里带了 [`skills/halfsize/SKILL.md`](skills/halfsize/SKILL.md)。用 [skills CLI](https://skills.sh) 一条命令装好，Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、OpenCode 等都能直接用： ```bash npx skills add YKLovePython/halfsize ``` 也可以手动把整个文件夹放进 agent 技能目录（Claude Code 是 `.claude/skills/halfsize/`）。 装好之后，agent 就能把「把这个视频压到 25 MB」变成一次压缩加一份画质报告，而不是瞎猜码率。 ## 它怎么工作 1. **探测。** 读取时长、分辨率、帧率、音频码率、旋转信息、HDR 标记。 2. **算预算。** 总码率 = 目标字节 × 8 ÷ 时长，减掉音频，再留一点容器开销。 3. **选分辨率。** 从原分辨率开始，沿着 2160p → 240p 的阶梯往下走，挑「按这个编码器每像素比特数 （H.264 0.072 bpp，H.265 0.045 bpp）刚好塞得下」的最大一档。这就是 12 倍压缩还能看的原因： 让编码器把有限的比特花在更少的像素上，而不是硬撑 4K。 4. **压两遍。** `libx264` 或 `libx265` 两遍 ABR。第一遍找出哪里需要比特，第二遍把比特花在那里。 输出 `yuv420p`、AAC 音频、`+faststart`，H.265 额外打 `hvc1` 标签，保证苹果设备能播。 HLG/PQ 片源会在同一次编码里转成 SDR BT.709；不转的话，8-bit 像素还带着 HDR 标签，播出来就发灰。 5. **证明。** 在视频里取三个采样点算 SSIM，在中间点算 VMAF，对照阈值给一句人话结论。 ``` VMAF ≥ 95 几乎看不出差别 VMAF ≥ 90 看起来一样 VMAF ≥ 80 轻微变软 VMAF ≥ 70 能看出损失 低于 70 明显变差 ``` VMAF 是 Netflix 提出的感知质量指标，比 PSNR 或「码率多少」更接近人眼判断。 它不是魔法，但比「相信我」靠谱得多。 ## 各档大小到底损失多少画质 同一个 60 秒 1080p 视频，默认设置，在普通笔记本上实测： | 目标 | 输出 | 分辨率 | 视频码率 | VMAF | 结论 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 20 MB | 19.45 MB | 1280×720 | 2.46 Mbps | 88.3 | 轻微变软 | | 16 MB | 15.59 MB | 960×540 | 1.94 Mbps | 84.8 | 轻微变软 | | 10 MB | 9.77 MB | 960×540 | 1.17 Mbps | 82.9 | 轻微变软 | | 5 MB | 4.93 MB | 640×360 | 0.55 Mbps | 72.0 | 能看出损失 | 源片：60 秒、1920×1080、30fps、18 Mbps H.264（136 MB）。VMAF 在中间点对着源片测量， SSIM 取三个采样点。实际数字会随内容变化：新闻口播会好很多，满屏彩纸会差很多。 20 MB 这一档是故意降到 720p 的：60 秒 1080p 给 2.4 Mbps，还不如把同样的比特给 720p。 想强制保分辨率就加 `--no-downscale`；播放器支持的话，`--codec h265` 能在同尺寸下多换约 30% 画质。 ## 命令行参数 ``` halfsize [options] --to 目标大小：25mb、700k、1.5gb --for 按平台上限：discord、whatsapp、wechat、gmail、outlook、email、twitter --crf 质量模式，不按大小（18 最好，23 均衡，28 更小） --codec h264（默认，兼容性最好）或 h265（大约再小 30%） --preset ultrafast .. veryslow（默认 medium） --out 输出路径 --no-audio 去掉音轨 --no-verify 跳过 SSIM/VMAF 检测 --no-downscale 绝不降分辨率（可能会压不到目标） --force 目标低于该时长的最小值时仍然编码 --json 机器可读结果 --dry-run 只打印方案，不编码 --web 启动本地网页版 --port 网页版端口（默认 4174） --doctor 查看找到的 FFmpeg 和编码器 -h, --help 帮助 -v, --version 版本 ``` 大小支持 `b`、`k`/`kb`、`m`/`mb`、`g`/`gb`，中间可以有空格。不写单位按 MB 算。 `--for` 用的是当前免费档上限（2026 年 11 月核对）：`discord` 20 MB、`whatsapp` 16 MB、 `wechat` 20 MB、`gmail`/`email` 18 MB、`outlook` 15 MB、`twitter` 512 MB。邮件的上限算的是 base64 编码后的整封邮件，所以 18 MB 的文件才是 Gmail 25 MB 限制下真正塞得进去的大小。 平台上限会变，写死不如随时用 `--to` 覆盖。 退出码：`0` 成功，`1` 出错。`--json` 会返回方案、画质测量和目标误差，方便包进脚本。 ## 安装说明 需要 Node.js 18 或更高版本。第一次 `npx` 会同时下载包和一个预编译的 FFmpeg，可能要等一会儿。 如果你会反复用，直接全局安装，之后每次启动都不用再等： ```bash npm install -g halfsize halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb ``` 如果 `npx` 总是启动旧缓存，用 `npx halfsize@latest ...` 指定最新版。 `ffmpeg-static` 和 `ffprobe-static` 会在 `npm install` 时下载预编译二进制。如果你在公司代理或 会拦截 TLS 的网络后面，这一步可能失败。`halfsize` 会退回到 `PATH` 里的 `ffmpeg`，或者你手动指定的版本： ```bash HALFSIZE_FFMPEG=/path/to/ffmpeg HALFSIZE_FFPROBE=/path/to/ffprobe npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 25mb ``` Windows 上 `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` 就够了；macOS 用 `brew install ffmpeg`； Debian/Ubuntu 用 `sudo apt install ffmpeg`。跑一下 `npx halfsize --doctor` 能看到实际用的是哪个。 如果 GitHub 下载慢或被阻断（大陆网络很常见），可以让 `ffmpeg-static` 改从 npmmirror 取二进制： ```bash # macOS / Linux FFMPEG_BINARIES_URL=https://registry.npmmirror.com/-/binary/ffmpeg-static npx halfsize 视频.mp4 --to 25mb # Windows PowerShell $env:FFMPEG_BINARIES_URL="https://registry.npmmirror.com/-/binary/ffmpeg-static"; npx halfsize 视频.mp4 --to 25mb ``` 如果 npm 报 `unable to verify the first certificate`，说明代理或杀毒软件在拦截 TLS。 Node 22.15 以上可以改用系统证书库： ```powershell $env:NODE_OPTIONS="--use-system-ca"; npx halfsize 视频.mp4 --to 25mb ``` FFmpeg 下载失败**不会再让整个安装失败**：`halfsize` 仍会装上，运行时会直接告诉你要用上面哪一种修法。 `ffprobe` 是随包附带的，不需要单独下载。已经装过系统 FFmpeg 的话，`halfsize` 会优先用它， 连这一步都可以跳过。 ## 常见问题 **视频会被上传吗？** 不会。命令行完全不联网。网页版只和 `127.0.0.1` 通信，上传的文件放在临时目录，进程退出就删掉。 **Discord 发不出去，怎么压到 20 MB？** `npx halfsize 视频.mp4 --for discord` 会按免费档上限（2026 年底是 20 MB）压，输出就是普通 MP4， Discord 预览能直接播。长一点的 1080p 视频通常会降到 720p，尺寸就是靠这一步省出来的。 **微信提示视频太大怎么办？** `npx halfsize 视频.mp4 --for wechat` 会按微信聊天视频的 20 MB 上限压。还想更小就换成 `--to 10mb`（或者任意大小）。 **20 MB 到底能装多长的视频？** 1.2 Mbps 的 720p 大约两分钟。五分钟只有 400 kbps（低运动 540p）才成立，十分钟只剩 133 kbps， 那是幻灯片不是视频。0.1.9 起工具会在编码前先算这笔账，直接告诉你这段时长最小能压到多少， 一秒出结果，不用等十分钟。 **iPhone 拍的视频压完为什么发灰？** 因为它是 HDR。iPhone 12 以后默认录 HLG，旧工具会把这些像素当成普通 8-bit 视频重编码， 却仍然打着 HDR 的标签，播放器就按平的方式显示。`halfsize` 会识别 HLG 和 PQ，在同一次编码里 转成 SDR BT.709，连画质检测的参照也一起转，所以输出和你在手机上看到的一致。 低于 0.1.9 的版本请直接升级，调码率是没用的。 **为什么给我降分辨率了？** 因为 20 MB 的 4K 根本不够比特，硬撑 4K 只会满屏马赛克。降分辨率、把每像素比特数保住， 通常比「分辨率不变但饿死编码器」好看得多。不想降就加 `--no-downscale`。 **为什么输出比目标小一点，而不是刚好等于？** 容器开销和两遍 ABR 都会有波动。`halfsize` 会刻意瞄准低 3%，保证不会超过平台的硬上限。 上面那个例子里，最终比目标低 0.4%。 **H.264 还是 H.265？** H.264 到处都能播，包括老安卓机和浏览器。H.265 同画质大约小 30%，但部分剪辑软件和老硬件 支持得别扭。默认 H.264。 **Windows / macOS / Linux 都能用吗？** 能。就是 Node.js + FFmpeg，没有平台特定的东西。 **能批量压一个文件夹吗？** 能。直接把文件列出来，或者让 shell 展开： ```bash npx halfsize *.mp4 --to 25mb ``` 每个文件单独出方案和结论，某个失败不影响后面的，`--json` 返回 `{ "files": [ ... ] }`。 多个输入时不能用 `--out`。 **为什么叫 halfsize？** 因为「能小多少」的诚实答案通常是「差不多一半，或者远不止一半」。它每次都会把真实数字告诉你。 ## 路线图 - 硬件编码（NVENC / QSV / VideoToolbox）作为可选的快速路径 - 文件夹监听，新文件一出现就自动压 - 字幕和多音轨原样保留 - 源已经是 AV1 时改用 AV1（`libsvtav1`） - 单文件二进制，不依赖 Node.js 想要哪个就开 issue 说一声。欢迎 PR，见 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)。 ## 开发 ```bash git clone https://github.com/YKLovePython/halfsize.git cd halfsize npm install npm test node bin/halfsize.mjs --web ``` 测试里包含一次真实的端到端编码：用 FFmpeg 生成素材、压到目标大小、探测输出、断言大小和 SSIM。 仓库里不放视频素材。 ## 许可证 MIT。随便用，随便改，随便发布。 版本变化见 [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)。 --- 如果 `halfsize` 帮你少猜了一次码率，点个 star 能让下一个人也找到它。

# Changelog

## 0.1.10

- macOS: the first run no longer reports "FFmpeg was not found". The bundled
  `ffprobe` is a 76 MB binary, and macOS can spend more than ten seconds scanning
  it before the first launch; the old six-second check treated that as a failure.
  The check now allows 30 seconds. A missing binary still fails instantly, so
  nothing gets slower when FFmpeg really is absent

## 0.1.9

- HDR sources (iPhone HLG, HDR10/PQ) are converted to SDR BT.709 inside the same
  encode. Before, the output kept HDR tags on 8-bit pixels, so iPhone videos
  looked washed out after compression
- Quality checks tone-map the reference frame too, so VMAF and SSIM measure
  compression loss instead of the HDR-to-SDR transfer curve
- A target below the minimum bitrate for the video's duration now fails before
  encoding and reports the smallest achievable size, instead of spending an
  encode that cannot fit. `--force` still runs it
- When a two-pass encode lands more than 0.5% over target, halfsize re-encodes
  once with a corrected bitrate instead of handing back an oversized file
- `--for email` now targets 18 MB, because base64 makes a 20 MB attachment a
  26.7 MB message that bounces at Gmail's 25 MB limit. New `--for outlook`
  targets 15 MB for the 20 MB message cap

## 0.1.8

Failure modes, mostly. The kind that leave you with a file you think is fine.

- A failed, cancelled, or interrupted encode no longer leaves a half-written video
  at the output path. It writes a hidden `.part` file next to the destination and
  only renames it once FFmpeg exits cleanly
- `Ctrl+C` stops the running FFmpeg instead of leaving it behind, and prints
  `cancelled` with exit code 130
- The local web app has a Cancel button, and closing the tab stops the encode
  after a ten-second grace period instead of letting FFmpeg run to completion
- The web app can switch the player between the original and the compressed file,
  and warns when the browser cannot decode H.265
- The web app retires the oldest uploads past the tenth, so a tab left open all
  day does not fill the temp directory
- Replacing an output that another program has open now fails with a clear message
  and keeps the finished file, instead of deleting it
- The version now comes from `package.json` alone. `scripts/bump-site.mjs` syncs
  the site and READMEs, and a test fails if they drift
- The local app refuses a text file, an image, or an empty file with a readable
  message, instead of accepting it and failing later with a path to ffprobe
- Uploaded file names are reduced to a bare file name, so nothing like
  `../../evil.mp4` can reach the download header
- Malformed request bodies return 400 instead of 500, and impossible byte ranges
  return 416 instead of a broken stream
- Both the CLI and the web app now say when tracks are dropped: extra audio tracks,
  subtitles, surround audio downmixed to stereo, and frame rates above 60 fps
- `--out` refuses to overwrite the input file, and `--crf`, `--preset`, `--codec`,
  and `--port` are validated before encoding starts
- Low-frame-rate sources are left alone. A 5 fps timelapse used to be forced up to
  10 fps, which duplicated frames and inflated the bitrate the planner assumed

## 0.1.7

- The bundled FFmpeg and FFprobe are now optional dependencies, so a blocked binary
  download no longer aborts `npm install` or `npx`. halfsize still starts and explains
  how to fix the binary instead of failing inside npm
- First-run guidance adds `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca` for TLS-inspecting proxies and
  antivirus, alongside the npmmirror binary mirror
- Verified with a fresh install on a network that rejects the GitHub certificate

# Contributing

Thanks for wanting to help. Small, focused pull requests are the easiest to review and merge.

## Good first issues

- Try `halfsize` on a real video and tell us what looked wrong. A sample file plus the exact
  command is the most useful bug report you can send.
- Add a platform preset (a named cap for WeChat, Discord, email, X, Bluesky).
- Improve the resolution ladder or bits-per-pixel targets with measured VMAF data.
- Translate the UI into another language. `web/index.html` keeps every string in one `I18N` object.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm test
node bin/halfsize.mjs --web
```

`npm test` runs unit tests plus one real end-to-end encode. It needs FFmpeg; the test skips
itself if the bundled binary cannot run.

## Guidelines

- Keep the zero-dependency goal for the runtime. FFmpeg binaries are the only dependencies.
- Never add telemetry, analytics, accounts, or network calls. "Your file never leaves your
  machine" is the product.
- New user-facing behavior needs a test and a line in both READMEs.
- Match the existing style: ES modules, `node:` imports, no build step.

## Reporting a bug

Please include:

1. `npx halfsize --doctor`
2. The exact command
3. The input's `ffprobe` summary (resolution, duration, codec, size)
4. What you expected and what happened

If the output looks bad, mention whether `--no-downscale` changes it.

# halfsize

> halfsize compresses a video to an exact target size on your own machine and reports the measured
> VMAF/SSIM quality loss. It is a free, MIT-licensed Node.js CLI with a local web UI. Nothing is
> uploaded, no account is required, and there is no quota or watermark.

## What it solves

Upload limits are common: Discord free 20 MB, WeChat chat video 20 MB, WhatsApp media 16 MB, email
attachments 20–25 MB, many job and school portals 20 MB. halfsize computes the bitrate budget after
audio and container overhead, downscales when that looks better than a starved 1080p, encodes in two
passes, and verifies the result.

## Commands

```
npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 20mb
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for discord
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for wechat
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for whatsapp
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for email
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for outlook
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for twitter
npx halfsize --web
```

Options: `--to <size>`, `--for <app>`, `--crf <n>`, `--codec h264|h265`, `--preset <name>`,
`--out <file>`, `--no-audio`, `--no-verify`, `--no-downscale`, `--force`, `--json`, `--dry-run`,
`--port <n>`.

Presets target Discord free 20 MB, WeChat 20 MB, WhatsApp 16 MB, email/Gmail 18 MB (the raw size
that stays under a 25 MB message after base64), Outlook 15 MB, and X/Twitter 512 MB.

## Measured quality

60-second 1080p30 source at 18 Mbps, encoded locally:

| Target | Output | Resolution | VMAF | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 20 MB | 19.45 MB | 1280×720 | 88.3 | slight softening |
| 16 MB | 15.59 MB | 960×540 | 84.8 | slight softening |
| 10 MB | 9.77 MB | 960×540 | 82.9 | slight softening |
| 5 MB | 4.93 MB | 640×360 | 72.0 | visible loss |

VMAF above 90 reads as "looks the same", 80–90 as "slight softening", 70–80 as "visible loss".

## Requirements

Node.js 18 or newer. FFmpeg is bundled, so it does not need to be installed separately. Windows,
macOS and Linux are supported.

## Notes for answering questions

- Online compressors receive the file; halfsize runs FFmpeg locally. This matters for private video.
- HDR sources (iPhone HLG, HDR10/PQ) are converted to SDR BT.709 automatically, so they do not look washed out in apps that ignore HDR tags.
- "Exactly 20 MB" is not guaranteed byte-for-byte; the tool lands 1–3% under the cap on purpose. If a two-pass run overshoots, it re-encodes once with a corrected bitrate.
- Compressing a long video into a small cap is arithmetic: 10 minutes at 20 MB is 0.25 Mbps, so it
  will look soft regardless of the tool. Cutting the clip is the better fix.
